page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-64 is a compute-focused instance within the general-purpose N2 machine series. It is powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon x86_64 processor offering 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via two threads per core with dedicated allocation. The configuration provides 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Cache architecture consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 33 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 VNNI, AES cryptography extensions, and bit-manipulation features such as BMI2 and ADX. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput and high memory bandwidth alongside moderate single-thread execution. The instance posted top-quartile results in large-block uncached memory operations, reaching 211.46 GB/sec in read bandwidth and 92.34 GB/sec in write bandwidth, as well as PassMark database operations (22021.79) and extended instruction tests (52333.77). Multi-core benchmarks sit comfortably within mid-tier performance envelopes, including a stress-ng multi-core metric of 59511.84 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12016.0. Single-core processing is comparatively constrained, with stress-ng single-core performance falling into the lower quartile at 1411.19 and single-threaded gzip compression at 23.8 GB/sec.

Because the server allocates 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, it delivers cost efficiency for CPU-dense workloads that do not demand extensive memory footprints. Relying on remote persistent disks introduces I/O considerations, as no local NVMe storage is bundled. The instance is suitable for parallel batch computing, distributed compilation, video encoding, microservices orchestration, and compute-bound API backends.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-64 is an Intel Xeon-based instance offering 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores at 2.8 GHz and 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a lean 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 support, it features 33 MB of L3 cache and delivers high uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 211 GB/sec for reads and 92 GB/sec for writes. The machine has no integrated local storage or GPU hardware. While single-thread benchmarks place toward lower percentiles, multi-threaded CPU and vector workloads perform consistently well. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for compute-intensive tasks where high core density is prioritized over expansive memory capacity, making it a reliable fit for software compilation, data transformations, and parallel microservice workloads.
